Information Law & Governance

Information law — confidentiality, consent, data protection and health records governance.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • State the importance of confidentiality
  • Describe consent and data protection principles
  • Explain health records governance

In simple terms

Information law and governance protect patient information — who can see it, how it is used and how long it is kept. Confidentiality is a core duty of nurses.

Key laws and principles: consent, data protection, confidentiality and records retention.

Confidentiality and consent

  • Confidentiality: do not share patient information without permission or legal authority.
  • Consent: get permission before sharing information or using it for purposes other than care.
  • Minimum necessary: share only what is needed for the purpose.

Data protection and governance

  • Store records securely (locked cabinets, password-protected computers).
  • Keep records for the required retention period.
  • Dispose of records securely (shredding, secure deletion).
  • Report breaches immediately.
  • Follow hospital policy and applicable data-protection law.

🔴 Confidentiality

Protect patient confidentiality — share information only with authorised people and only what is needed for care.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Documentation — record only relevant information; store records securely.
  • Communication — do not discuss patients in public areas; share only with the care team.
  • Consent — get permission before sharing information outside the care team.
  • Records — keep records for the required time; dispose securely.
  • Breaches — report lost, stolen or improperly accessed records immediately.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Confidentiality protects patient information from unauthorised access.
  2. Get consent before sharing information for purposes other than care.
  3. Share only the minimum necessary information.
  4. Store records securely and keep them for the required retention period.
  5. Report confidentiality breaches immediately.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Do not discuss patients in public areas (lifts, corridors, cafeterias).
  2. Lock computers and paper records when not in use.
  3. Follow hospital policy and data-protection law.
  4. Dispose of records securely (shredding, secure deletion).

📌 Memory trick

Confidentiality: “N-M-S” — Name the need, Minimum necessary, Share with care team only.

60-second revision

  • Information law protects patient information.
  • Confidentiality, consent, minimum necessary.
  • Store securely; keep for retention period; dispose securely.
  • Report breaches immediately.
  • No discussing patients in public.

Test yourself

Confidentiality means:

Answer: B. Confidentiality means protecting patient information and sharing only with authorised people.

Before sharing information outside the care team, get:

Answer: B. Get consent before sharing information for purposes other than care.

Records should be kept:

Answer: B. Keep records for the required retention period, then dispose securely.

If records are lost or accessed improperly, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Report confidentiality breaches immediately.

Minimum necessary means:

Answer: B. Share only the minimum information needed for the care purpose.
